Releases are cut by pushing a git tag named `vYYYY.MM.N`, for example `v2026.09.2`. CI then builds and publishes. Never publish by hand. This comes from a stored project convention in EngramDB.

The steps:

1. Pick the next tag. `N` is the release counter within that month. `pyproject.toml` currently says `version = "2026.9.1"`, so the next September release would be `v2026.09.2`. October releases would start at `v2026.10.1`. I'm assuming `N` starts at 1 each month, since the memory only gives one example.
2. Make sure `main` is clean and the tests pass. The repo has a convention to run them with `make test-fast`.
3. Create and push the tag, for example `git tag v2026.10.1 && git push origin v2026.10.1`.
4. Let CI build and publish.

I found nothing else about releases in the repo: no CI workflow files, no changelog, no release doc, and no release or publish target in the `Makefile`. So I can't confirm what CI does after the tag is pushed. I also can't tell whether you're meant to bump `pyproject.toml` before tagging. The version string there uses `2026.9.1` without a zero pad, while the tag format uses `2026.09.2`.

I haven't tagged or pushed anything.
